relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project statement that materializes the raw output row geometry from attacker-controlled TIFF tags. In the staged witness, the surrounding block fixes the destination to width 1, height 65312, and `cpp = 1` for the later lossless-JPEG decode.

`parseSOF()` validates only the generic JPEG range and header shape, so it accepts a two-component lossless-JPEG frame even though the already-parsed destination row length is one pixel. The vulnerable source never enforces the missing obligation `sof->cps <= mRaw->dim.x` before the frame becomes reachable to `decodeN<2>()`.
Second-row predictor reload. With `predNext` still pointing at the previous one-pixel row and `N_COMP == 2`, this copy reads across the row's lone 2-byte pixel into ASan-poisoned padding.

edges.description: The component count admitted at `parseSOF()` is carried through `frame.cps` and selects `decodeN<2>()`, so the same count becomes the `copy_n()` read width at the sink.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `sof_component_guard.jpeg_component_count == predictor_copy_sink.copy_component_count == 2`; the same equality remains true in the genuine witness case `imagewidth2_cps2_boundary`.

edges.description: After the first decoded row sets `predNext = dest`, the same previous-row start pointer is reused unchanged as `predNext` at the second-row predictor reload.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `prednext_alias.row_start_ptr == predictor_copy_sink.prednext_ptr` on the crashing path, proving the second-row sink reloads from the first row start pointer.
